prompt: A quilter sews a seam connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangular patch. That seam measures $9$ inches. How many inches long is the third side of the patch — the one the seam does not touch?
hint: A segment joining two midpoints of a triangle is called a midsegment.

hints.text: A segment joining two midpoints of a triangle is called a midsegment.
The Midsegment Theorem: the midsegment is parallel to the third side and exactly HALF its length.
If half the third side is 9, the third side is $2 \times 9 = 18$ inches.

explanation: The seam joins the midpoints of two sides, so it is a midsegment.
By the Midsegment Theorem, a midsegment is half the length of the third side.
The seam is 9 in, so the third side is $2 \times 9 = 18$ in.

alternativeExplanations.title: Which direction to go
steps: Ask which measurement you have: the short one (midsegment) or the long one (third side)?
You have the short one, so you MULTIPLY by 2 rather than divide: $9 \times 2 = 18$ inches.
